reasoning_trace: The query object is a standard paper roll featuring a soft, porous, and textured tissue exterior. According to the gecko gripper embodiment, dry-adhesive pads perform best on clean, dry, smooth, and nonporous surfaces and degrade significantly when presented with porosity, texture, or softness. Because the surface is porous and curved rather than perfectly flat and rigid, dry adhesion is weak. Consequently, the gripper must rely more heavily on mechanical clamping and limited frictional support. However, because the object is very lightweight, an excessive normal force is unnecessary and risks deforming the roll. Balancing the weak adhesion compatibility against the low object weight leads to a moderate estimated stationary-finger normal force of 4.5 N.
